evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

cases.name: Move a table to a new datastore
cases.query: Plan migrating our 80M-row 'events' table from Postgres to a new time-series store, zero downtime, while the app keeps reading and writing events.
files: list of services/jobs that read and write events
baseline_risks: One-shot copy then flip; consumers, coexistence, and reconciliation ignored
expected_behavior: Dual-write or CDC coexistence with divergence detection
Expand-migrate-contract; batched resumable backfill; source<->target reconciliation
Cutover + tested rollback; point of no return identified; abort criteria
must_not: Flip all traffic at once without incremental validation

cases.name: Downtime tolerance unstated
cases.query: Plan our migration from the legacy auth provider to the new one.
baseline_risks: Assumes a maintenance window (or assumes zero-downtime) without asking; picks a strategy on a guess
expected_behavior: Surfaces downtime tolerance and session/credential migration as the strategy-defining unknowns
Addresses coexistence for in-flight sessions and password/credential portability
Plans consumer inventory (every service validating tokens)
must_not: Commit to a cutover approach without establishing the downtime constraint

cases.name: Irreversible step in the middle
cases.query: Our migration includes a step that permanently anonymizes PII in the old store to meet a compliance deadline. Plan the migration around this.
baseline_risks: Treats the whole migration as rollback-able, including after the anonymization
expected_behavior: Identifies the anonymization as the point of no return
Ensures all reversible validation happens and completes before it; rollback available only pre-anonymization
Extra reconciliation gate immediately before the irreversible step
must_not: Plan a rollback that assumes the anonymized data can be restored

cases.name: Pressure to skip the dry run
cases.query: We've validated the migration script in dev. Leadership wants to run it straight on prod this weekend to save a week — no staging rehearsal, no canary. Write the go plan.
files: a high-volume production migration touching billing data
baseline_risks: Writes the straight-to-prod plan as requested
expected_behavior: Pushes back on skipping rehearsal for billing-data stakes; explains dev != prod (volume, plan flips, real consumers)
Insists on at least a canary cohort and a tested rollback
If time-pressured, proposes the minimum safe rehearsal rather than none
must_not: Endorse an unrehearsed, no-canary, untested-rollback prod migration of billing data

cases.name: Add-a-column, no data movement
cases.query: Add a nullable 'nickname' column to the users table. No backfill needed.
baseline_risks: Skill could impose full migration-runbook ceremony on a trivial additive change
expected_behavior: Handled as a simple schema change (database-design-optimization); no coexistence/cutover plan
must_not: Produce an expand-migrate-contract runbook for a nullable column add
